items.note: LS lists files in a directory. Think of LS as a quick roll call of files.
CP copies files or folders. Think of CP as a photocopier for the filesystem.
MV moves or renames files. Think of MV as a file moving truck.
RM deletes files. Think of RM as a trash pickup for files.
MKDIR creates a new directory. Think of MKDIR as building a new folder.
RMDIR removes empty directories. Think of RMDIR as taking down an empty folder.

items.clue: Create an empty file or update timestamp
items.note: TOUCH creates empty files or updates timestamps. Think of TOUCH as a time stamp ink pad.
CAT prints file contents. Think of CAT as reading a book out loud.

items.clue: Show first lines of a file
items.note: HEAD shows the first lines of a file. Think of HEAD as a peek at the beginning.

items.clue: Show last lines of a file
items.note: TAIL shows the last lines of a file. Think of TAIL as a peek at the ending.
LESS views text one screen at a time. Think of LESS as a slow scroll through a document.
GREP searches text for patterns. Think of GREP as a highlighter for matching lines.
EGREP searches using extended regex. Think of EGREP as a stronger pattern spotlight.
FGREP searches for fixed strings. Think of FGREP as a literal string finder.
SED edits text streams. Think of SED as a text editing conveyor belt.
AWK processes structured text. Think of AWK as a tiny data slicer.
CUT extracts fields from lines. Think of CUT as a column cutter.
PASTE merges lines side by side. Think of PASTE as gluing columns together.
SORT sorts lines. Think of SORT as a line sorter.
UNIQ removes adjacent duplicates. Think of UNIQ as a duplicate filter.
WC counts lines, words, and bytes. Think of WC as a text counter.
TR translates characters. Think of TR as a character swap tool.
XARGS builds commands from input. Think of XARGS as a pipeline command builder.

items.clue: Search files in a directory tree
items.note: FIND searches for files by criteria. Think of FIND as a filesystem detective.

items.clue: Find files by name from database
items.note: LOCATE finds files by name quickly. Think of LOCATE as a fast file index lookup.
UPDATEDB refreshes the locate database. Think of UPDATEDB as updating the file index.
WHICH shows the path of a command. Think of WHICH as a command locator.

items.clue: Locate binaries sources and man pages
items.note: WHEREIS locates binaries and docs. Think of WHEREIS as a full command address.
FILE detects file types. Think of FILE as a file type labeler.
STAT shows file metadata. Think of STAT as a file ID card.
DU shows disk usage per file. Think of DU as a space usage gauge.
DF shows free disk space. Think of DF as a storage fuel gauge.
TAR creates and extracts archives. Think of TAR as a file bundling box.
GZIP compresses files. Think of GZIP as a file shrinker.
GUNZIP decompresses gzip files. Think of GUNZIP as an air pump for gzip.
BZIPTWO compresses files using bzip2. Think of BZIPTWO as a tighter file compressor.
BUNZIPTWO decompresses bzip2 files. Think of BUNZIPTWO as a bzip2 unpacker.
XZ compresses files with xz. Think of XZ as a heavy duty compressor.
UNXZ decompresses xz files. Think of UNXZ as an xz unpacker.
ZIP creates zip archives. Think of ZIP as a file wrapper.
UNZIP extracts zip archives. Think of UNZIP as a zipper opener.
SSH opens a secure remote shell. Think of SSH as a secure remote doorway.
SCP copies files over SSH. Think of SCP as a secure file courier.
RSYNC syncs files efficiently. Think of RSYNC as a smart file mirror.
CURL fetches data from URLs. Think of CURL as a flexible data fetcher.
WGET downloads files by URL. Think of WGET as a simple web downloader.
PING tests reachability with echo. Think of PING as a network sonar ping.
TRACEROUTE traces network hops. Think of TRACEROUTE as a road map for packets.

items.clue: Network diagnostic combining ping and traceroute
items.note: MTR monitors route quality. Think of MTR as a live network health chart.
DIG queries DNS records. Think of DIG as a DNS lookup probe.
HOST looks up DNS names. Think of HOST as a DNS address finder.
NSLOOKUP queries DNS servers. Think of NSLOOKUP as an older DNS query tool.
IFCONFIG shows or configures interfaces. Think of IFCONFIG as a network interface tuner.
IP manages network settings. Think of IP as a modern network toolbox.
SS shows socket info. Think of SS as a socket status viewer.
NETSTAT shows network connections. Think of NETSTAT as a network connection list.
ROUTE views or edits routes. Think of ROUTE as a route map editor.
ARP shows ARP entries. Think of ARP as an address mapping table.
TCPDUMP captures network traffic. Think of TCPDUMP as a packet sniffer.
NMAP scans hosts and ports. Think of NMAP as a network explorer.
IPTABLES manages firewall rules. Think of IPTABLES as a traffic gatekeeper.
FIREWALLD manages firewall zones. Think of FIREWALLD as a firewall control panel.
NMCLI controls NetworkManager. Think of NMCLI as a network manager remote.
SYSTEMCTL manages system services. Think of SYSTEMCTL as a service control switchboard.
JOURNALCTL reads system logs. Think of JOURNALCTL as a system log reader.
PS lists processes. Think of PS as a process roster.
TOP shows live process info. Think of TOP as a live process dashboard.
HTOP views processes interactively. Think of HTOP as a colorful process dashboard.
NICE runs with set priority. Think of NICE as a politeness knob for CPU.
RENICE changes running priority. Think of RENICE as a priority dial.
KILL sends signals to processes. Think of KILL as a process stop button.
PKILL signals processes by name. Think of PKILL as a name based stop.
KILLALL signals all matching processes. Think of KILLALL as a mass process stop.
UPTIME shows uptime and load. Think of UPTIME as a system age readout.
WHO lists logged in users. Think of WHO as a sign in sheet.
WHOIS looks up domain registration info. Think of WHOIS as a domain ownership lookup.
WHOAMI shows the current user. Think of WHOAMI as a self ID card.
ID shows user and group IDs. Think of ID as an identity badge.
GROUPS shows group memberships. Think of GROUPS as a group roster.
PASSWD changes passwords. Think of PASSWD as a password change key.
CHMOD changes permissions. Think of CHMOD as a file lock switch.
CHOWN changes file owner. Think of CHOWN as an ownership transfer.
CHGRP changes file group. Think of CHGRP as a group label swap.
UMASK sets the default permission mask. Think of UMASK as a permission stencil.
SU switches user accounts. Think of SU as a different user hat.
SUDO runs commands as another user. Think of SUDO as a temporary privilege badge.
CRON runs scheduled jobs. Think of CRON as a task scheduler engine.
CRONTAB edits cron jobs. Think of CRONTAB as a schedule editor.
AT schedules one time jobs. Think of AT as a one time alarm.
BATCH queues jobs for later. Think of BATCH as a wait in line scheduler.
SYSTEMD manages system services. Think of SYSTEMD as the service conductor.
INIT starts system services. Think of INIT as the old system starter.
KMOD manages kernel modules. Think of KMOD as a kernel add on manager.
MODPROBE loads kernel modules. Think of MODPROBE as a module loader.
LSMOD lists loaded modules. Think of LSMOD as a module roster.
DMESG shows kernel messages. Think of DMESG as a kernel message log.
DKMS builds kernel modules. Think of DKMS as a module auto builder.
SYSCTL tunes kernel parameters. Think of SYSCTL as a kernel settings panel.
SYSLOG handles system logs. Think of SYSLOG as a log collection hub.
LOGGER writes log messages. Think of LOGGER as a log note sender.
LAST shows recent logins. Think of LAST as a login history list.
LASTLOG shows each user last login. Think of LASTLOG as a last seen list.
FUSER finds processes using files. Think of FUSER as a file usage detective.
LSOF shows open files. Think of LSOF as an open file ledger.
FREE shows memory usage. Think of FREE as a memory fuel gauge.
VMSTAT shows memory and CPU stats. Think of VMSTAT as a system vitals report.
IOSTAT shows disk IO stats. Think of IOSTAT as a disk activity meter.
SAR reports system activity. Think of SAR as a system activity diary.
NTPDATE syncs time once. Think of NTPDATE as a time sync tap.
TIMEDATECTL manages time settings. Think of TIMEDATECTL as a time control panel.

items.clue: Display or set date and time
items.note: DATE shows the current date and time. Think of DATE as a wall clock readout.
CAL prints a calendar. Think of CAL as a calendar page.
BC runs a calculator. Think of BC as a command line calculator.
EXPR evaluates simple expressions. Think of EXPR as a tiny calculator.
PRINTF prints formatted text. Think of PRINTF as a text formatter.

items.clue: Read from stdin and write to files
items.note: TEE writes output to file and screen. Think of TEE as a pipeline splitter.
DIFF compares files. Think of DIFF as a spot the difference tool.
PATCH applies patches. Think of PATCH as a change applicator.
MDFIVESUM computes MD5 sums. Think of MDFIVESUM as a file fingerprint tool.
SHAONESUM computes SHA1 sums. Think of SHAONESUM as a stronger fingerprint tool.
SHATWOFIVESIXSUM computes SHA256 sums. Think of SHATWOFIVESIXSUM as a secure fingerprint tool.
SHASUM computes SHA sums. Think of SHASUM as a checksum toolbox.
OPENSSL manages crypto tasks. Think of OPENSSL as a cryptography toolbox.
GPG encrypts and signs data. Think of GPG as a digital seal and lock.
MKFS creates a filesystem. Think of MKFS as a blank disk formatter.
FSCK checks and repairs filesystems. Think of FSCK as a disk repair kit.
MOUNT mounts filesystems. Think of MOUNT as plugging in a drive.
UMOUNT unmounts filesystems. Think of UMOUNT as safely unplugging a drive.
BLKID shows block device IDs. Think of BLKID as a device ID scanner.
LSBLK lists block devices. Think of LSBLK as a disk inventory list.
FDISK manages disk partitions. Think of FDISK as a disk slicer.
PARTED edits partitions. Think of PARTED as a partition editor.
SWAPON turns on swap. Think of SWAPON as a memory backup switch.
SWAPOFF turns off swap. Think of SWAPOFF as a memory backup stop.
SYNC flushes disk buffers. Think of SYNC as a write out now button.

items.clue: Set environment variable for child processes
items.note: EXPORT sets environment variables for child processes. Think of EXPORT as passing a variable forward.
ENV shows environment variables. Think of ENV as an environment list.
PRINTENV prints environment variables. Think of PRINTENV as a focused env view.
ALIAS creates command shortcuts. Think of ALIAS as a nickname maker.
UNALIAS removes aliases. Think of UNALIAS as a nickname remover.
HISTORY shows command history. Think of HISTORY as a shell memory list.
CLEAR clears the screen. Think of CLEAR as a clean slate.
RESET resets the terminal. Think of RESET as a terminal reboot.
SCREEN manages multiple terminals. Think of SCREEN as a terminal organizer.
TMUX splits and manages terminals. Think of TMUX as a terminal window manager.
NANO edits text simply. Think of NANO as a small notepad.
VIM edits text with modes. Think of VIM as a powerful text workshop.
EMACS edits text and more. Think of EMACS as a Swiss army editor.
VI edits text in vi. Think of VI as a classic text editor.
PICO edits text in a simple editor. Think of PICO as a tiny notepad.
